summary: Round 4's stated fixes are real and verified live: git -C/--git-dir and gh --repo/-R global-flag-prefixed invocations are now correctly detected and blocked, matching the PR's claims, and the task-registry cross-reference sensibly reduces reliance on the cgroup-name-pattern check alone. However, live reproduction against the committed snippet with the exact targeted git 2.43 found a real, previously undisclosed bypass that this round's subcommand-scanning rewrite does not address: git and gh alias expansion. Running `git config alias.p push` (an entirely ordinary, common user customization, not an adversarial trick) then `git p origin master` passes straight through the wrapper unblocked and performs a real push to origin/master (verified end to end against a real bare repo: the push landed, exit 0, no BLOCKED message), because _interactive_guard_git_find_subcommand() only recognizes the literal token 'push' and has no knowledge of ~/.gitconfig's [alias] section -- the alias name (e.g. 'p') is treated as an unrecognized subcommand and let through, while the real git binary still silently expands and executes the alias. The identical class of gap applies to gh via `gh alias set`. This is exactly the kind of 'real, non-obscure' bypass this task's own stated bar is supposed to catch (rounds 2-4 all rejected similarly ordinary bypasses: command git, spoofed INVOCATION_ID, global flags), and unlike the honestly-disclosed residual gaps (absolute-path invocation, command -p, systemd-run impersonation, version-tied flag allowlist), this one is not mentioned anywhere in the extensive KNOWN LIMITATIONS section despite being at least as easy to trigger. Given this PR's explicit charter is closing real bypasses in a security-critical guard and disclosing what remains, shipping without addressing or at minimum disclosing the alias-expansion gap undermines the round's core deliverable.
issues: Live-reproduced bypass: `git config alias.p push` followed by `git p origin master` is not detected by _interactive_guard_git_find_subcommand() (it only matches the literal 'push' token) and the push reaches the real origin/master unblocked -- verified against the real git 2.43 binary and a real bare repo, not simulated.

The same alias-based bypass class applies to gh (`gh alias set` can rename `pr merge` to an arbitrary alias), which _interactive_guard_gh_is_merge()/_interactive_guard_gh_strip_globals() cannot recognize since they only match literal 'pr'/'merge'/'api' tokens.

This gap is not disclosed anywhere in the KNOWN LIMITATIONS section, unlike every other residual bypass in this file (absolute-path invocation, command -p, systemd-run impersonation, version-tied global-flag allowlist), breaking the round's own standard of honest disclosure of what remains open.
No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff, so the hard no-workflow-file rule from SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md does not apply here.
